summary: Ruth says to Naomi let me go to field glean after him in whose eyes I find favor, Naomi says go my daughter, Ruth goes, happens to come to part of field belonging to Boaz who is of Elimelech's family. Boaz comes from Bethlehem, says Yahweh be with you to reapers, they answer Yahweh bless you, Boaz asks whose young woman is this? Foreman says Moabite woman who returned with Naomi, asked please let me glean, has been from morning till now. Boaz says to Ruth: don't go glean in another field, keep close to my young women, I commanded young men not touch you, when thirsty go to vessels and drink. Ruth falls on face why have I found favor you take notice of me since I am foreigner? Boaz says I have been told all you did to mother-in-law how you left father mother land and came to people you did not know. Yahweh recompense your work, full reward under wings you have taken refuge. Ruth asks may I continue to find favor, you have comforted. At mealtime Boaz says come eat dip morsel in vinegar, she sits beside reapers he reaches parched grain she eats satisfied leaves. Boaz commands let fall some bundles deliberately leave, don't rebuke. She gleans ephah of barley, returns to Naomi shows, Naomi says blessed be he, has not left off kindness to living and dead, man is near kinsman. Ruth says he said keep close to young men until harvest finished, Naomi says good my daughter go with his young women not in another field. So Ruth kept close until end barley and wheat harvests dwelt with mother-in-law.
whyItMatters: Ruth's loyalty meets Boaz's kindness, gleaning law in action, wings refuge, and kinsman introduction. Shows providence — happens to come to Boaz's field.

keyVerses.text: May Yahweh repay your work, and a full reward be given to you from Yahweh, the God of Israel, under whose wings you have come to take refuge.”
keyVerses.why: Wings refuge — image of God as bird sheltering chicks and Boaz as agent.

keyVerses.text: She went, and came and gleaned in the field after the reapers; and she happened to come to the portion of the field belonging to Boaz, who was of the family of Elimelech.
keyVerses.why: Happened — chance but providence, Hebrew miqreh.

keyVerses.text: Then she fell on her face and bowed herself to the ground, and said to him, “Why have I found favor in your sight, that you should take knowledge of me, since I am a foreigner?”

questions.question: What is gleaning and why is Ruth allowed to glean?
questions.answer: Gleaning law Leviticus 19:9-10 and Deuteronomy 24:19-22 — landowners not reap to edges, not gather fallen, leave for poor and foreigner. Ruth as Moabite widow foreigner poor is exactly intended beneficiary. She says let me glean after him in whose eyes I find favor — acknowledges favor needed, not entitlement. Goes and happens to come to Boaz's field — Hebrew miqreh chance, but narrative hints providence guiding her steps to kinsman.

questions.question: What does 'under whose wings you have come to take refuge' mean?
questions.answer: Boaz says Yahweh God of Israel under whose wings you have come to take refuge — image of bird sheltering chicks under wings (Psalm 91:4). Ruth left father's house to take refuge under God's wings, and Boaz becomes human agent of that refuge by allowing gleaning close, protecting, providing water, food. Later Ruth asks Boaz spread wing/edge of garment over me (3:9) — same word kanaph — asking Boaz to embody prayer he prayed, be wings.

questions.question: Why does Boaz tell young men not touch Ruth and offer water from vessels?
questions.answer: Protective — field could be dangerous for young foreign woman alone, young men might harass. Boaz commands not touch (naga can also mean sexual touch), and offers water that young men drew — uncommon generosity, normally gleaners bring own water. Shows kindness beyond law. Ruth falls on face why favor foreigner? Boaz heard all she did — left father mother land to come to people not known — loyalty (hesed) recognized. Recompense and full reward prayed.

questions.question: What does letting fall bundles deliberately and ephah of barley indicate?
questions.answer: Boaz commands reapers pull out from bundles and leave deliberately for her to glean, don't rebuke — beyond gleaning law, extra generosity, leaving intentional. She gleans ephah of barley — about 22 liters, 30 pounds, over week's wages? Large amount, shows abundance. Returns to Naomi shows what gleaned and gives leftover from meal. Naomi says where gleaned today, blessed be he, has not left off kindness (hesed) to living and dead — hesed continues. Man is near kinsman, one with right to redeem (goel) — introduces next act.

glossary.def: Gather leftover after reapers, provision for poor and foreigner per Leviticus.
Chance, happened to — narrative hint of providence guiding steps.
Bird wings sheltering, also edge of garment — refuge image, Boaz as agent.
About 22 liters dry measure, ~30 pounds barley — large, abundant gleaning.
